en:
Yo.
I'm Makoto Shindo.
Truth is, I had a killer story saved up, but...
...this is bad.
Iwashita's story just now.
The one about the art club girl named Shimizu.
Thing is, I knew about that too.
No, wait, in my case it's a little different.
How do I know about all that, you ask?
It's a long, complicated story.
...It's kinda hard to say.
Let's just say a lot of stuff happened.{p}

What's wrong, {a}?
You scared?
You went to the art room earlier, right?
And you saw it, didn't you? That face.
That horrifying face from when she was killed.{p}You saw it, right?
I saw it
I didn't see it
I don't remember anymore

You didn't see it?
Come on, you don't have to lie to me of all people.{p}

Be honest.
I could see it too, you know.
What's the matter?
Are you scared?
The rumor says you're gonna die soon, so yeah, I guess you've got reason to be scared.
I've heard that rumor too.
They say all four of them really did die.{p}

...That's exactly why I figured I had to tell you, no matter what, before we're the ones who end up dead.
The other rumor about Tomoko Shimizu.{p}

So, you wanna hear it?
If you hear it, maybe you'll find some way to deal with this.{p}What'll it be?
I'll listen
I don't need to hear it

Okay.
Then I'll tell you the other story about Tomoko Shimizu.{p}

...Truth is, Shimizu's house was right near mine.
So I'd known her since way back.
To me, she was kind of like a sweet big sister.
She really loved painting.
I don't think she ever went out much, even on days off.
She stayed shut up in her house painting the whole time.
And on the rare days she did go out, it was to the park with a sketchbook to draw.
Her whole life was painting, no kidding.
Anyway, I used to go over to her house to hang out a lot.
Not like that, okay?
Don't get the wrong idea.
This was back when I was a little kid.
By the time I got to junior high, I never went into her room anymore.
And she'd stopped inviting a guy like me over, too.{p}

It was a real girl's room, I guess you'd say.
It had cute pink curtains, and everything was neat and tidy.
I can still remember that room clearly, even now.
But out of all my memories of her room, there's just one thing I can't stop thinking about, no matter what.{p}What do you think it was?
The room's decorations
The paintings kept in her room
The smell of the room
An album she treasured
See, it was the paintings she kept in her room.{p}

Well, she was painting all year round, so there were a crazy number of them.
It wasn't so much paintings hung up for decoration as the whole place just being covered in them.
And since everything was so neat and tidy, the atmosphere felt kind of abnormal.
The closet was crammed full of sketchbooks and canvases and stuff.{p}

She looked all embarrassed and said,
"Don't look,"
and I still can't forget it.
Naturally, she painted landscapes, portraits, still lifes, all kinds of stuff.
But there was one thing she was really fixated on and kept painting over and over.{p}Can you guess what it was?
Scenery of the places she always went on trips
A record of herself growing up
Her dead pets

She painted portrait after portrait of herself.
You could practically call it a record of her growing up.
She'd probably been painting them since she was old enough to remember.
You know how people keep photos of themselves from when they were little in an album?
In her case, it was paintings instead of photos, I guess.
And we're talking way more than your usual number, too.
She'd happily show me the pictures of herself she'd been piling up since she was small.
In a way, I guess it's kind of a creepy hobby.
Whenever she showed me her self-portraits, she looked really happy.
Maybe she wasn't really showing them to me.
Maybe she just used me as an excuse because she wanted to look at them herself.
She had this totally entranced look on her face.
She was basking in it.{p}

In a word, she was a narcissist.
The kind who looks at their own face in the mirror and gets lost staring at it.
You know people like that, right?
They're not even that cute or good-looking, but they never budge from in front of the mirror.
She was that type.
The mirror just turned into a painting, that's all.
Yeah, I can say it for sure.
It's not that she wanted to show me her paintings.
She painted self-portraits and looked at them because she wanted to admire herself.
Whether I was there or not didn't matter one bit.
After all, the only paintings she'd ever show me were the ones she painted of herself.{p}

Isn't that scary when you think about it?
She didn't love painting.
She loved herself, plain and simple.
No matter what she painted, it was just practice so she could paint herself better.
And she kept trying to paint an even more beautiful, more wonderful version of herself.{p}

...Sorry, I got kinda worked up.
...Maybe I'm actually scared too.
I mean, I saw that painting, the one the rumors say means you're gonna die.
Same goes for you, right, {a}?
And for the other five here, too.
...I told you earlier that I stopped going to her house once I got to junior high, right?
There's actually a reason for that.
The reason I stopped going to her house.
No, it'd be more accurate to say the reason she stopped inviting me.{p}What do you think it was?
You did something that made her hate you
You found out her secret
She got interested in something else

There was a reason she stopped inviting me over, see.
She got herself a boyfriend.
If you ask me, he was no looker at all.
He seemed smart enough, but he looked like a weakling.
If anything, he was the type delinquents pick on.
The type who runs crying to his parents the second he gets bullied, you know?
The type who gets through life leaning on other people and bowing to whoever's stronger.{p}

I don't know why Shimizu fell for that guy, or why they started going out.
I wasn't all that interested, so I don't even know his name.
But on days off, that guy would hang around at her house from morning till night.
I don't know what they were doing in there.
Well, I can pretty much guess.{p}

Seeing that, anybody'd get curious, right?
So I decided to do a little snooping on the sly.
Hey, back then I'd only just started junior high.
If anything happened, I could pass it off as a kid's prank.{p}Don't you want to know where those two met and how they started going out?
I want to know
I don't want to know
I'm not really interested
So first off, I decided to find out who the guy was.{p}

On a day off, I hid by the window in my house and watched her house all day long.
The guy showed up early in the morning, and he took so long to come out of the house that I started getting mad, wondering when he'd ever leave.{p}

I got sleepy, too.
I was only in junior high, after all.
By the time I rubbed my drowsy eyes and looked at the clock with my head all foggy, it was already past midnight.
That was way too late, any way you look at it.
I was just thinking, how could the parents put up with this, when he finally came out.{p}

So I tailed the guy right away.
I hadn't noticed during the day, but watching him walk at night, he was kind of like a sleepwalker.
Swaying, swaying, wobbling, wobbling, he walked like he was floating in the air.
It was creepy.
He looked like somebody was pulling his strings, too.
He'd stayed so late, his house had to be close by.
No way he'd be catching a train, I figured, and that put me a little at ease.{p}

The moment he turned right at a corner not far from my house, he was just gone.
Like smoke, I swear.
I was stunned.
And then this fear I can't even describe welled up inside me.{p}

...Can something like that even happen?
That guy was definitely not human.
Shimizu was going out with something that wasn't human.
After that, I quit following him.
Because I was scared.
...But it wasn't long after that.
Shimizu and that guy started fighting.
Even after all that, the one thing I didn't quit was watching her house.
On days off, I'd peek at her house from my window.{p}

That day, it wasn't even evening yet.
But even so, that guy came bursting out of the house.{p}

And right behind him, Shimizu came out, wailing and sobbing.
When people say someone's hair is flying wild and they're crying with their whole face, I guess that's the kind of face they mean.
And she was throwing the books and paints and stuff in her hands at him.
The guy was just smirking.
Smirking like he was making fun of Shimizu.{p}

"I'll kill you! Scum like you, I'll kill you!"
She screamed that and lunged at him.
I could hear it all the way over at my house.
Honestly, everybody in the nearby houses was craning their necks out their windows.
The guy dodged her, easy as anything, and muttered something.
I couldn't hear his voice, but it seemed to me like he was cursing her out.{p}

"Don't think I can't do it! Scum like you, I'll kill you!"
That was the first time I'd ever seen her look so terrifying.
She really looked like she'd kill him any second.
Even so, the guy just sneered and started wobbling off again.
She collapsed right there in tears.{p}
And after that, I never saw him again.{p}

About a month after that, she was murdered.
Somebody strangled her.
In fact, when she was killed, the police came around asking questions at my house and all over the neighborhood.
I kept my mouth shut, but somebody must've talked, don't you think?
About that guy.
It was that big of a fight, after all.
It wouldn't be strange if everybody remembered it.
Or if they'd told the cops about it, too.{p}

But there's no way they'd ever find him.
Because that guy wasn't human.
Here's what I think.
I think he was a person who doesn't exist.
So if the one who killed Shimizu was him, they'd never find him no matter how hard they searched.
No wonder the case went unsolved.{p}
...So, {a}?{p}How about we go to the art room one more time, right now?
I'll go
I won't go

Nobody cleared that painting away.
So it should still be there.
And it might still have that horrifying face.
You see, there's just one thing about that painting that's been bugging me.
I'm gonna go make sure of it right now.{p}

...Hm hm, {a}?
How does it look to you?{p}

Me, I'd say it looks like Shimizu's face when she was murdered.
Come on, let's get a closer look.{p}

...Just as I thought. It's exactly what I figured.
See, I've seen dozens of her self-portraits.
And I loved the self-portraits she painted.
The strange thing is, I never heard of her painting many portraits at school.
This was probably the first and last time she ever painted one outside her home.
So it's no wonder nobody noticed.
But you can't fool my eyes.{p}

...This painting, see, has been painted twice.
On this canvas, there's another picture hidden under her self-portrait.
The way it's laid on... the amount of paint...
That's not how she normally painted.
I bet she forced herself to paint the self-portrait to hide the real picture underneath.
It had nothing to do with the competition coming up or anything like that.
She painted this desperately, to hide something.{p}

What do you say, {a}?
Want to try scraping this painting?
We might get cursed.
But it might lay the truth bare in front of us.{p}What'll it be, {a}?
Leave it as it is
Try scraping off the paint

So you'll scrape it, huh.
Yeah, that's right. Even if we leave it like this, we're gonna die anyway.{p}

If we're gonna die either way, we'd better do everything we can.
All right, I'm scraping.{p}

...Look!
I knew it, there's something hidden underneath.
Come on, I'll scrape off some more.
I know what's painted here.
You know too, don't you?
There's no doubt about it.
She tried to seal this picture away so that guy wouldn't kill her.
That's it!
It's him!
The guy who was always hanging around her house was this man, no question.
The man who lives inside this painting!{p}

...You know, here's what I think.
I bet Shimizu was really lonely.
She must have wanted someone by her side all the time.
So she decided to create a man who'd stay with her forever.
Using the medium she was best at: painting.
I don't know what method she used, but anyway, I guess it worked.
Whether it was a ghost, a demon, or a delusion she created, I can't say.{p}

Still, she succeeded in calling up something nameless.
But that man did what she told him at first, and then gradually started defying her.
He got a will of his own, and started asserting it.
...And then tragedy struck.
When she tried to seal him inside the painting, he killed her.{p}
Even so, she must have kept coming back as a ghost day after day, finishing the painting little by little, trying to seal the man inside it.{p}

The four who died weren't cursed to death by her, but by the man in that painting.
Don't you think she was desperately trying to warn people about him, hoping someone would notice?
That the man in that painting existed, and how to get rid of him.
To stop that, he killed off the four guys who were close to learning the secret...
Don't you think so?
That's what I'd like to think.
Mind you, it's not like I actually know anything.
It's all just something I imagined.{p}

Anyway, I've wiped out the painting.
So there's no telling what happens from here.
Maybe, like the rumor says, we're going to be cursed to death by Shimizu sometime soon for seeing that painting.
But then again, now that the man's gone, maybe we don't have to worry about getting killed anymore.
Well, we'll know how it turns out soon enough.
Sometime soon.{p}

...Sometime soon.
Ha ha ha...{p}

Well then, let's head back to the newspaper club.
We've still gotta hear whoever's next.{p}

Figured as much.
Which means you're gonna die too.{p}

Don't get all sulky on me.
I saw it too, so we're in the same boat.{p}

...Heh, listen to you.
"I don't remember,"
you say?{p}You're seriously telling me you forgot already?
I really forgot
Actually, I remember

Huh, is that so.
Then there's nothing I can tell you.{p}

...No, wait, there is one thing.
Listen, you'd better take good care of your life while you can.
That rumor that anyone who sees the horrible face in that painting dies...
It's the real thing, you know.
With that, Shindo stood up.{p}

Looking angry, he walked off to the door.
What should I do? {f:He's going to leave|It looks like he's going home}.{p}{f:I|I}...
Let him go
Call him back

{f:I|I} watched Shindo leave.
I'd forgotten, and that was that{f:.|.}{p}
None of us felt like going on any longer, so in the end {f:we|we} just called it a day.{p}

When I got home to my room, {f:I|I} flopped down on my bed.
Honestly, thanks to Shindo, I'd botched the interview{f:.|.}
I'd have to get everyone together again sometime soon...
I was thinking about that when it happened.
{f:I|I} felt a strange gaze on me.
What {f:was it|could it be}?
{f:I|I} sat up and looked at the poster on the wall.
......Our eyes met.{p}

It was the poster that was looking at {f:me|me}☆
No, it was no longer {f:my|my} poster.{p}

The face still looked straight ahead, but its eyes alone rolled to glare at me.
This face......
{f:I|I} screamed.
This face, the one I'd just seen in the art room.
As {f:I|I} kept screaming in terror, the face pressed down on top of me.{p}

Everything went black before my eyes.
A lukewarm breath blew against my ear.{p}

"Come now... you're coming along too."
Was this the voice of the dead Shimizu{f:?|?}
At that instant, {f:my|my} arms rose.
They clamped down on my parched, bone-dry throat.
That's insane!
{f:My|My} arms were trying to strangle {f:me|me}★
I was slowly fading.
Giving {f:myself|myself} up to the swelling darkness, in the final moment I saw {f:my|my} own body, gone cold.{p}
That face looked exactly like the Shimizu I'd seen in the art room.........{p}

"Shindo!"
{f:I|I} stood up.
"{f:Sorry about that|I'm so sorry}.
The truth is, I did see it. But I was scared..."{p}

Shindo turned around.
"It's fine, I get how you feel. So, mind if I go on with the story?
It's another story about Tomoko Shimizu."
Of course, nobody was going to object.
When {f:we|we} nodded, Shindo sat back down in his seat.
All right, here goes.{p}

Thought so.
Once you've seen a face like that, there's no way you could ever forget it.{p}You really did see it, didn't you?
I saw it
I didn't see it

Shindo folded his arms as if to say the story was over, and looked around at {f:us|us}.
{f:I|I} was dumbfounded.
"That's... it?"
"You're not interested in Tomoko Shimizu's story, right?
I didn't bring any other stories."
He said it with a perfectly straight face.
But if the story about Shimizu was true, then Shindo, who said he'd seen that horrifying face too, had to be in danger{f:, didn't he?|, didn't he?}
"...Aren't you scared, Shindo?"{p}

When I asked that, he grinned.
"I'm the only one who won't die.
I was going to tell you why, but you said you didn't want to hear it."
The reason only Shindo wouldn't die★
"What the hell does that mean★"
Someone shouted.{p}

I caught up with Shindo as he walked down the hallway and put a hand on his shoulder.
Shindo turned around, annoyed.
"What? You've got no more business with me, right?"
"{f:It was my fault|It was my fault}. I apologize, so please come back to the club room and tell your story."
{f:I|I} bowed my head low.
But above {f:my|my} head, Shindo let out a little snort.{p}

"Too late. That's your punishment for throwing my kindness back in my face.
You're going to get Tomoko Shimizu's curse."
That was way too cruel!
{f:I|I} was apologizing with all my heart, and he was sneering at me like this.
The blood rushed to my head.
"Isn't that way too selfish★ As long as you're the only one who's saved, it's fine?!"{p}

"Shut up."
As he started to walk off, I frantically grabbed his arm.
"I said wait!"
"What the hell are you doing? Let go!"
Shindo shook his arm.
When he saw {f:I|I} still wouldn't let go, he {f:kicked his leg up at me|swung it around even harder}.{p}

"Ugh!"
{f:A brutal blow to my gut|His arm hit me}.
{f:I|I} couldn't take it and crumpled into a crouch.
"{f:That's what you get for being so damn persistent|Ah...}!"
{f:With that, Shindo started walking again, and I|Shindo} {f:glared at his back|looked flustered and started to walk away}.{p}

{f:Hatred|That one}{f: swelled up rapidly in my chest.| wasn't on purpose, I think.}
{f:As if driven by something,|But to just walk off}{f: I broke into a run.| without even apologizing...}{p}

The handle was slick with blood.
No way★
{f:I|I} peered into Shindo's face.
Smeared with the streams of blood running from his head, his half-open eyes didn't blink.
{f:I|I} had killed Shindo★
Everything around me started spinning, and {f:I|I} sank to the floor.{p}

It's actually the decorations in her room.
There were posters stuck up all over the walls of that room.
If they'd been idols or whatever, I'd have just thought, yeah, she's a girl after all...
But Shimizu's collection had no rhyme or reason at all.
Not just idols and anime, either. There were ones like some totally unknown enka singer, and pictures cut out of the calendars shops give away.
There was even an election poster, which surprised me. Who knows where she tore that one down from.
And the person on each one was always facing straight out.{p}

Thinking back now, I bet she always wanted someone to be watching her.
The whole time, from the moment she woke up in the morning until she went to bed at night.
Whenever I was in that room, my back always started crawling.
It was uncomfortable as hell, but she looked happy.
So I figured...{p}

maybe she picked a self-portrait for her entry in the prefectural competition because she wanted lots of people to see it.
But if that's so, why does that painting turn into a horrifying face?
Once a rumor about a curse gets started, nobody's going to want to look at it.
There's no way she could stand that.
And yet......
Could it be she's got something she's trying to say?{p}What do you think?
That can't be it
I think she's got something she's trying to say

...Yeah, you're right.
I guess that's way too far-fetched.
...Sorry, but could you let me rest a little?
My head's getting all jumbled. I don't even know what I was trying to say anymore.
Maybe I can talk more later, but give me a break for now.
...No, wait, just one last thing.{p}

If Shimizu comes to see you, say, tonight... I'm just saying.
No matter what she looks like, could you try not to be scared of her?
I think that'd be a terrible insult to her.
I don't want you lumping her in with yokai and evil spirits.
I bet that's how the four who died got killed.
So, yeah.
And one more thing... if you can, would you tell her I've been wanting to see her?
Weird, huh?
She might be an evil spirit, and I still want to see her.
But...... I'm counting on you.
That's it for my story, for now.
Who's up next?{p}

So you think so too!
Then come with me to the art room!
If we go back there one more time, I know I'll hear her voice.
I can hear out whatever it is she's trying to say.{p}

...You've got a look on your face like you're wondering why I'm so into this.
I told you, didn't I? We were neighbors.
But that's not all.
Well, I guess you could say I kind of had a crush on her...
She was someone special to me.
Tch, don't make me say dumb stuff like that.{p}

...Okay, we're here.
I'm opening the door.{p}

...Good, the painting's just like it was before.
Go on, get closer and take a look.
...That's it.
I don't know what it looks like to you.
But I can see bitter regret in her face.
Come on, Shimizu!
If there's something you want to say, then say it!{p}

............I can hear a voice.
It's Shimizu's voice!
You understood me, didn't you, Shimizu!
Thank god.........{p}

...See, {a}? Can you tell?
The painting's gone back to the beautiful Shimizu it used to be, right?
Shimizu says she was lonely.
Her bitterness at being murdered and her anger at everyone who avoided her turned the painting into that thing.
But it's all right now.
The painting's back to normal, after all.
I don't think you guys are going to die now either. Probably.{p}

...What did I do, you ask?
I just told her that if she was lonely, she could come with me.
She was happy about it.
Can't you see her?{p}

Shimizu's right here on my shoulder now.
You look like you've got a strong sixth sense, so I figured you'd be able to see her.
I don't care if she's an evil spirit.
From now on, I'm going to be with Shimizu forever......
Well then, let's head back to the newspaper club.
We've got to hear the next guy's story.{p}

It was the smell of her room, see.
Sort of a sickly-sweet smell.
But that wasn't all.
If you paid attention, there was a faint stench too, kind of rank, the kind that makes the back of your throat sting.
Maybe the sweet smell was perfume to cover up the stench.
Anyway, it always bugged me.
One day, I'd gone over to her room to hang out like always.
She went out, saying she'd bring me some juice.{p}So there I was, left alone. What do you think I did?
You sniffed the painting in her room
You opened her desk drawer

There was a half-finished canvas in her room.
I thought it might be the source of the stench, so I put my nose up close to it.
......I thought I caught a faint whiff.
But I couldn't really tell.
The smell of the oil paint was too strong, that clammy, kerosene-like smell.
Just then the door opened, and she came in carrying a tray.{p}
So I never did find out what it was.{p}

But I'll never forget that smell.
I know now: it smelled like tanned leather.
I don't know why something like that would be in her room, though.
Sometimes I wonder if she was into black magic or something.{p}

Like maybe the four who died were killed by black magic too.
Anybody know how to break a witch's curse?{p}

...Of course you wouldn't know.
Looks like my story was a waste of time.
I thought maybe there was a chance of breaking her curse.
Well, nothing we can do about it.
Which of us is gonna die first, you or me... or maybe we'll go together.
Either way, you'd better hurry up and make your peace with it.
That's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}

I had a feeling the stench was coming from her drawer.
So I quietly opened it.
The second I did, a foul reek hit my nose.
That smell.
It took everything I had not to throw up.
Then I worked up the nerve and peered inside.{p}

What do you think was inside...?
Thin, tightly rolled-up things, kind of like paper.
There were tons and tons of them in there.
I figured they had to be the stuff you paint on... canvas, right? That stuff.
I knew she painted, after all.
But the stench seemed to be coming from those canvases.
I nervously reached out.
The instant I touched one, I knew what it was.
It wasn't cloth.
And it definitely wasn't paper.
It was the skin of something.
That's where the stench was coming from.{p}

Just then, a hand came down on my shoulder.
Shimizu had come back without me noticing, and she was standing there with a terrifying look on her face.
Holding a tray with juice and an apple on it.
"So you've seen them."
That's what she murmured.
Her usual gentle air had vanished without a trace.
"These are my treasures. The skins of the things I love most.
When I use them as canvases and paint on them, the inspiration just wells up."{p}

She had a paring knife clenched in her hand.
"I adore you too, you know. I meant to wait a little longer for the right time, but......"
The knife glinted.
"Give me your skin!"
She thrust the knife at me, and on instinct I rolled sideways and dodged it.{p}

Her face right then was just like a witch's.
I got scared and shoved her as hard as I could.
And while she was off balance, I bolted out of the room.
Even after I'd run all the way home, my heart kept pounding for a good while.
Was that who she really was?
Behind all that kindness, had she been waiting for her chance to skin me?
Thinking about it scared me so bad that for a while I had nightmares.
We never got together again after that.
I kept away from her, and whenever we ran into each other on the street, she'd ignore me.{p}

...Looking back now, I wonder if that really happened.
Maybe she was just messing with me.
But what if those things in the drawer really were skin?
What if she really was trying to skin me......{p}

That self-portrait of hers must have been painted on one of those canvases too.
Isn't that why she kept trying to finish it even after she became a ghost? Because she didn't want anyone to find out?
If people learned where her inspiration really came from, they might come to loathe her work itself, and throw it out or burn it.
I think that's what she feared most.
But a ghost's hands couldn't give it a proper finish.{p}

That painting turning into a horrifying face was meant to scare people so nobody would look at it.
Even so, I bet the four who were killed were the ones who noticed something was off.{p}

...Of course, that's just a guess.
But I'm pretty confident in this theory.
After all, I actually saw those canvases with my own eyes.
So even if you've seen that face, I don't think you'll die, as long as you don't notice the canvas.
Feel better?
...Can't blame you if you don't.
I mean, I just went and blabbed it all to you right now.
